canonical_definition:
What it is. Most papers treat GLUE as a benchmark suite, or collection, of diverse natural language understanding tasks, often described as covering sentence-level classification, inference, paraphrase, similarity, sentiment analysis, textual entailment, and linguistic acceptability. A recurring framing is that it is a multi-task evaluation benchmark, sometimes even an analysis platform, though papers differ on its exact composition: several describe nine tasks, others refer to eight tasks or datasets, and many use subsets such as four binary classification datasets, five challenging tasks, or six selected subtasks. A smaller line of work describes it more narrowly as shorter-sequence NLU evaluation, as a source of classification and entailment tasks, or as including question answering and coreference resolution.

What it is claimed to measure. Papers use GLUE mainly to measure natural language understanding. It is linked to 10 constructs and 9 behavioral indicators overall, and the most recurrent additional uses are for text classification, language understanding task performance, sentiment analysis, and natural language inference. The claims therefore converge most clearly on natural language understanding, while smaller lines of work also report GLUE as measuring broader or neighboring targets.

Space of uses. Across papers, GLUE is commonly used as a main evaluation benchmark for fine-tuning or downstream assessment, and authors often report average GLUE scores or results on selected GLUE tasks rather than always using the full suite. It is linked to 8 measurement instruments overall, most often through task-level components such as SST-2, MRPC, QNLI, QQP, and RTE. Papers also use it as a general capability check after model editing, compression, pruning, or distillation, and in a few cases with zero-shot or 2-shot prompting setups.

Concerns raised. Only a few papers raise explicit concerns about GLUE itself. One paper mentions GLUE as a knowledge-based or logic-based benchmark and treats it as not capturing nuanced human preferences.

characterization_sections.label: What it is.
characterization_sections.text: Most papers treat GLUE as a benchmark suite, or collection, of diverse natural language understanding tasks, often described as covering sentence-level classification, inference, paraphrase, similarity, sentiment analysis, textual entailment, and linguistic acceptability. A recurring framing is that it is a multi-task evaluation benchmark, sometimes even an analysis platform, though papers differ on its exact composition: several describe nine tasks, others refer to eight tasks or datasets, and many use subsets such as four binary classification datasets, five challenging tasks, or six selected subtasks. A smaller line of work describes it more narrowly as shorter-sequence NLU evaluation, as a source of classification and entailment tasks, or as including question answering and coreference resolution.

characterization_sections.label: What it is claimed to measure.
characterization_sections.text: Papers use GLUE mainly to measure natural language understanding. It is linked to 10 constructs and 9 behavioral indicators overall, and the most recurrent additional uses are for text classification, language understanding task performance, sentiment analysis, and natural language inference. The claims therefore converge most clearly on natural language understanding, while smaller lines of work also report GLUE as measuring broader or neighboring targets.

characterization_sections.label: Space of uses.
characterization_sections.text: Across papers, GLUE is commonly used as a main evaluation benchmark for fine-tuning or downstream assessment, and authors often report average GLUE scores or results on selected GLUE tasks rather than always using the full suite. It is linked to 8 measurement instruments overall, most often through task-level components such as SST-2, MRPC, QNLI, QQP, and RTE. Papers also use it as a general capability check after model editing, compression, pruning, or distillation, and in a few cases with zero-shot or 2-shot prompting setups.

characterization_sections.label: Concerns raised.
characterization_sections.text: Only a few papers raise explicit concerns about GLUE itself. One paper mentions GLUE as a knowledge-based or logic-based benchmark and treats it as not capturing nuanced human preferences.
